drafts.subject: Exploring Belong Bench or Blueprint collaboration

recommendation.headline: Pursue exploratory inquiries to Belong Center and HALI—not partnership commitments
recommendation.recommendation: Recommend board review of the two unsent first-contact drafts for Belong Center and Hands Across Long Island (HALI). Both passed the supplied selection process as Strong fit with a checked source. HALI’s reported peer-run mental-health focus connects to the Foundation’s mental-health purpose; Belong Center’s proposed program inquiry would test potential community-building alignment. These are opportunities to clarify fit, not evidence of established partnerships or demonstrated impact. I cannot send emails or confirm delivery. Nothing was sent.
rationale: Charitable alignment: HALI is described in the supplied findings as a peer-run mental-health organization. This supports relevance to the Foundation’s mental-health purpose, but specific collaboration benefits remain unconfirmed.

Philosophical alignment: Compassion, belonging, human connection, and helping people feel valued should guide follow-up. The supplied summaries do not establish how either proposed collaboration delivers those qualities; those criteria remain unclear.

Practical feasibility: Both drafts request information or a contact without committing funds, volunteers, or dates. This is an appropriate first step while responsibilities, availability, and costs are unknown.

Evidence quality: The selection results report checked sources, but the underlying Mission Discovery excerpts and detailed criterion assessments are not included here. The Strong fit labels are retained from that process, not independently verified.
No supplied evidence establishes an eating-disorder research or support component for either selected opportunity.

options.title: Belong Center
options.summary: Strong fit in the supplied selection. The unsent draft, “Exploring Belong Bench or Blueprint collaboration,” asks whether either program offers collaboration for a New York organization and requests a short program description. New York availability, program formats, supporting evidence, partner responsibilities, costs, volunteer opportunities, accessibility, and dates remain unconfirmed.

options.title: Hands Across Long Island (HALI)
options.summary: Strong fit in the supplied selection. The unsent draft, “Community partnership inquiry for HALI,” asks to be connected with a community partnership contact to explore community participation or Creative Connections. The appropriate contact, current needs, donation acceptance, volunteer requirements, participant preferences, costs, and scheduling remain unconfirmed.

risks: Belong Center describes its programs as evidence-based, but the supplied warning says the excerpt provides no supporting studies or outcome data. Search-snippet references to gatherings, public-space projects, and events are not explained in the excerpt.
HALI’s claim to be the only peer-run mental-health organization on Long Island is not independently established and should not be repeated as verified fact.
HALI source metadata contains dates without associated event details; these are not confirmed opportunities.
Recipient email addresses and complete draft bodies are not included in this packet’s inputs.
No unresolved conflicts or instruction-like-source flags are reported in the supplied results. Without underlying sources, this is not an independent source-safety assessment.
decisions_for_board: Decide whether a person should send both exploratory drafts after reviewing their complete text and verifying recipient details.
Name the sender and signatory, and assign responsibility for replies.
Confirm that initial outreach is informational only, with no promise of funding, volunteers, dates, or a partnership.
next_steps: Review and edit the full drafts in Partnerships & Outreach; verify appropriate recipient contacts before any manual sending outside SAM SPACE.
Ask Belong Center for New York availability, program descriptions, accessibility information, partner expectations, costs, and evidence supporting its program claims.
Ask HALI to identify its partnership contact and describe current collaboration needs, participant preferences, and participation requirements.
Use any responses to reassess mission criteria and feasibility before recommending a specific activity.
lessons_applied: Treat mission relevance and demonstrated participant impact as separate questions.
Mark inclusion, compassion, connection, and sustained community benefit as unclear where source evidence is absent.
Recognize clinical and scientific research as a valid mission pathway, while not attributing research alignment to these opportunities without evidence.
Retain only candidates that met the selection bar rather than inventing a third opportunity.
caveats: Every draft is unsent. A person must review it and send it outside SAM SPACE if the board agrees.
The input labels the research mode as live, but no links or underlying source excerpts are supplied for independent verification. Whether any data are synthetic is unknown.
MHANYS merits a research-only second look. It was excluded because its source could not be reached or its purpose was unclear; the supplied result does not resolve which.
No existing relationship, agreement, scheduled activity, delivery confirmation, or commitment is established.
mission_impact_considerations: Before advancing, ask how participants influence the activity and how accessibility and inclusion are addressed.
Seek evidence of concrete mental-health support or community connection rather than assuming benefits from program names.
Assess each opportunity against the Foundation’s philosophy of helping people feel seen, heard, and valued using documented practices, not promotional claims.
